summary: Reads MIDI note, controller, program change, pitch wheel, timing, system, and file events into CHOP channels.
key_concepts: Reads MIDI note, controller, program change, pitch wheel, timing, start/stop/continue, song position, and system-exclusive events from devices, internal sources, or MIDI files.
Simplified Output automatically creates channels for every received MIDI event type, so the channel set expands as a device is used.
Multiple MIDI CHOPs can read from the same or different sources, and Channel Prefix controls whether MIDI channel streams are split or merged.
Controller Format supports normal 7-bit controllers or paired 14-bit controller messages with documented MSB and LSB index rules.
MIDI values are saved in the .toe and restored on reload, which can cause jumps when physical controllers are in different positions.
Low Sample Rate settings can miss rapid on/off events; higher rates or Preserve Pulses help represent dense MIDI activity.

common_gotchas: Simplified Output dynamically expands channel count as event types are received; downstream schemas should tolerate changing channels.
MIDI values are saved into the .toe and restored on reload, but physical controller positions may differ and jump when moved.
Multiple MIDI CHOPs can read the same or different sources, so shared device access is possible but may duplicate events.
MIDI Start/Stop/Continue can control the Timeline/Beat Dialog when configured, which can affect global project timing.
Use MIDI In Map CHOP when portability through the MIDI Device Mapper matters more than direct channel/note/controller addressing.
For event-table workflows, consider MIDI In DAT or MIDI Event DAT instead of CHOP channels.
Low sample rates can miss or collapse fast note on/off pairs; use a sufficiently high sample rate for performance control or switch to MIDI In DAT for exact event ordering.
14-bit controller data requires paired MSB/LSB controller messages; enabling 14-bit behavior without a matching controller pair can produce no useful output.
Do not assume raw OS device names are enough for live MIDI; TouchDesigner MIDI workflows commonly depend on the MIDI Device Mapper and the selected device/id mapping.
